rulings.challenge_claim: The row's parenthetical attributes the vav-prefixed אל token to oshb:Eccl.5.1, but the only vav-prefixed instance sits at oshb:Eccl.5.5; the row also omits a hevel-family token in its own closing verse (Eccl.5.6) that sibling row p02-004 discloses at its own hevel site.
rulings.grounds: Byte tier, re-derived independently from verse_map_oshb.json word splits (not retyped): oshb:Eccl.5.1 = אַל ... אַל -- BOTH occurrences are bare (patach, no vav); the vav falls on וְלִבְּךָ֧ ("and your heart"), not on either אל. The vav-prefixed form is at oshb:Eccl.5.5's second occurrence: אַל ... וְאַל. The row's parenthetical "twice, including the form with the vav-prefix" attached to oshb:Eccl.5.1 is therefore a real locative misattribution; the 5-tokens/3-verses arithmetic itself is correct. Separately, oshb:Eccl.5.6 -- this row's OWN closing verse -- carries וַהֲבָלִ֔ים, a hevel-family token (eccl_device_inventory.json hevel_refrain.attested_forms.והבלים = ["Eccl.5.6"], confirmed by direct byte read of the verse); the tier-1 inventory's by_chapter.5 = 2 names exactly oshb:Eccl.5.6 and oshb:Eccl.5.9 as the two chapter-5 sites, and the sibling row p02-004 discloses its own hevel site (oshb:Eccl.5.9) explicitly while this row discloses neither its misattributed location nor its own hevel token -- the standing SYMMETRY-completion rule (a sweep, not a spot fix) is unmet on this row's own side.
rulings.remedy: Correct the parenthetical to read: oshb:Eccl.5.1 carries two bare אל tokens; the vav-prefixed וְאַל sits at oshb:Eccl.5.5's second occurrence. Add the hevel-family disclosure for this row's own closing verse oshb:Eccl.5.6 (וַהֲבָלִ֔ים) to device_notes/observed_substrate_signals, matching the symmetry already given by p02-004 at oshb:Eccl.5.9. Test: collate.py byte-tier match of the corrected parenthetical against oshb:Eccl.5.1 and oshb:Eccl.5.5; confirm both chapter-5 hevel_refrain sites are named across their owning rows.

rulings.challenge_claim: Same locative misattribution as LF's item (converges on the vav-prefix error), plus: the patach-pointed negative chain the row treats as closing its own unit continues one verse past the row's own rear seam, and two further root-level continuities cross that same seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGES with the LF item on the core defect (independently re-verified: oshb:Eccl.5.1's two אל tokens are bare; the vav-prefixed form is at oshb:Eccl.5.5). DISTINCT addition, byte-confirmed: the same patach-pointed negative particle continues at oshb:Eccl.5.7 -- אַל תִּתְמַ֖הּ ("don't marvel") -- one verse past this row's own rear seam (the row's own span ends web:Eccl.5.7 = oshb:Eccl.5.6). Two further undisclosed root-level continuities cross that same seam: חֵ֖פֶץ (oshb:Eccl.5.3, inside this row's own span) and הַחֵ֑פֶץ (oshb:Eccl.5.7, the immediate neighbor) share the chet-pe-tsade root; and שְׁמֹ֣ר (this row's OWN opening imperative, oshb:Eccl.4.17) and שֹׁמֵ֔ר (oshb:Eccl.5.7) share the shin-mem-resh root. None of these three is disclosed. The row's framing that the negative chain 'holds the unit together... closes on a motto rather than a new topic' before web:Eccl.5.8 overstates what the particle-chain alone shows -- the chain does not itself terminate at the row's close. The boundary conclusion is NOT overturned: the fear-God motto close, כִּ֥י אֶת הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְרָֽא (oshb:Eccl.5.6), is an independent, byte-sound warrant that the row still carries, and the campaign's own CROSS-SEAM COHESION rule treats an undisclosed byte-true device straddling a seam as a disclosure defect, not automatically a boundary refutation.
rulings.remedy: Disclose that the patach-pointed אל chain continues one verse past this row's own close (אַל תִּתְמַ֖הּ עַל הַחֵ֑פֶץ at oshb:Eccl.5.7), and disclose the חפץ (oshb:Eccl.5.3 / oshb:Eccl.5.7) and שמר (oshb:Eccl.4.17 / oshb:Eccl.5.7) root echoes as texture, while keeping the fear-God motto (oshb:Eccl.5.6) as the row's actual, sufficient boundary driver. Test: confirm the revised rationale no longer implies the negative-particle chain itself terminates cleanly at the row's own close; collate.py byte-tier check on the added quote.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's isolation ground -- "nothing in the verse shares vocabulary with either neighbor" -- is byte-false against the front neighbor on three counts (חפץ root, שמר root, and the negative-particle chain).
rulings.grounds: Byte tier, independently re-verified: הַחֵ֑פֶץ (oshb:Eccl.5.7, this row) and חֵ֖פֶץ (oshb:Eccl.5.3, inside the preceding row's own span) share the chet-pe-tsade root. שֹׁמֵ֔ר (oshb:Eccl.5.7) and שְׁמֹ֣ר (oshb:Eccl.4.17, the preceding row's OWN opening imperative) share the shin-mem-resh root. אַל תִּתְמַ֖הּ (oshb:Eccl.5.7) is the sixth token of the same patach-pointed negative chain the preceding row's own admonition rests on. All three are real root-level continuities the row's unqualified "shares no vocabulary with either neighbor" (rationale and rejected_alternative, both) does not survive. The senses do differ (vow-context "delight" vs. an official's "watching duty"; an imperative "guard" vs. a participle "watcher/overseer"), so the ISOLATION RESULT is not itself overturned by texture-level root echoes, but the row's stated GROUND is inaccurate as written. Separately, the device_notes' "don't marvel" observation (אַל תִּתְמַ֖הּ) is boundary-relevant Hebrew texture given only in English gloss, with no pointed splice -- an ENGAGEMENT CLASS gap.
rulings.remedy: Re-state the isolation ground as root-qualified rather than absolute: disclose the חפץ and שמר root echoes with oshb:Eccl.5.3 and oshb:Eccl.4.17 as texture that does not overturn the isolation (different senses named). Add a pointed byte-tier quote for the "don't marvel" clause (אַל תִּתְמַ֖הּ, oshb:Eccl.5.7) to device_notes. Test: collate.py byte-tier match for the added quote; confirm neither the rationale nor rejected_alternative asserts a total absence of shared vocabulary.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row twice mislabels the oshb:Eccl.5.10 ketiv/qere as sitting on a pronoun when its own quoted run shows a construct noun; the refrain-tag placement is misdescribed; and the rear-boundary "no lexical link" ground is refuted on both sides of that seam.
rulings.grounds: GRAMMAR CHECK, independently re-derived: the row's own byte-tier run at oshb:Eccl.5.10 is ראית רְא֥וּת עֵינָֽיו -- ketiv ראית, qere רְא֥וּת, a construct/verbal noun ("the seeing of") governing עֵינָֽיו ("his eyes"). This is not a pronoun; the clause's only pronominal element is the suffix on עֵינָֽיו itself, which carries no K/Q note. The row's boundary_rationale calls the note-bearing word "the pronoun," and device_notes repeats the same characterization for the same verse -- a doubled grammatical mischaracterization confirmed against the row's own spliced bytes; oshb:Eccl.5.8's actual pronoun K/Q (היא / ה֑וּא, on this cluster's own p02-003 row) is the plausible source of the conflation. PLACEMENT: גַּם זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל (oshb:Eccl.5.9) is verse-final, following BOTH the loves-silver clause and the loves-abundance (אֹהֵ֥ב בֶּהָמ֖וֹן) clause -- confirmed by direct word-index read -- not "closing its own opening clause" as the row states; it closes the whole verse. REAR-BOUNDARY: the row's "lacking a lexical link to loves/satisfied/advantage" ground (rationale and rejected_alternative) is refuted at root level on both fronts -- יִשְׂבַּ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.5.9, this row) and וְהַשָּׂבָע֙ (oshb:Eccl.5.11, the very next row) share the שבע ("satisfied") root; אוֹכְלֶ֑יהָ (oshb:Eccl.5.10, this row) and יֹאכֵ֑ל (oshb:Eccl.5.11) share the אכל ("eat") root. Additionally the hevel by_chapter digit is cited without naming its numbering space (MT vs. WEB ch.5) though the digit is 2 in both spaces here, so that piece is a disclosure gap, not an arithmetic error.
rulings.remedy: Correct BOTH mislabeled instances (boundary_rationale and device_notes) of the oshb:Eccl.5.10 K/Q word רְא֥וּת: relabel as a construct/verbal noun ("seeing of," governing עֵינָֽיו), not a pronoun. Correct the גַּם זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל placement description to "verse-final, closing the whole verse." Qualify the rear-boundary claim to disclose the שבע and אכל root continuities into oshb:Eccl.5.11 as texture not overturning the row's own pairing. Name the numbering space for the hevel by_chapter digit. Re-examine the medium confidence rating against the book plan's own low-confidence flag for the MT 5:8-9 difficult-syntax-plus-K/Q region. Test: standard Hebrew grammatical review confirms the corrected part-of-speech label; collate.py byte-tier re-check of all quotes.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's sole boundary ground -- "shares no content token with either neighbour" -- is byte-false on both the front and rear sides, and is asserted without a named swept object or digit.
rulings.grounds: Byte tier, independently re-verified. FRONT: וְהַשָּׂבָע֙ (oshb:Eccl.5.11, this row) and יִשְׂבַּ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.5.9, p02-004's span) share the שבע ("satisfied/satiety") root; יֹאכֵ֑ל (oshb:Eccl.5.11) and אוֹכְלֶ֑יהָ (oshb:Eccl.5.10, p02-004's span) share the אכל ("eat") root. REAR: לֶֽעָשִׁ֔יר (oshb:Eccl.5.11, "to the rich [man]") and עֹ֛שֶׁר (oshb:Eccl.5.12 = web:Eccl.5.13, the opening word of the very case narrative the row calls unrelated) share the ע-ש-ר root ("rich/riches," different lexemes -- adjective vs. abstract noun -- but the same root, which is also the semantic hinge the WEB rendering itself trades on: from the rich man's sleeplessness to riches kept to their owner's harm). The row's rationale and rejected_alternative both state the unqualified "shares no content token" claim with no swept object named and no digit, which the campaign's count-object discipline requires. The device_notes' negative claim (no hevel/tachat-hashemesh refrain attaches here) is independently confirmed correct -- neither inventory lists oshb:Eccl.5.11.
rulings.remedy: Replace the unqualified "shares no content token" claim with a root-qualified statement: disclose the שבע root shared with oshb:Eccl.5.9 and this row's own וְהַשָּׂבָע֙; the אכל root shared with oshb:Eccl.5.10 and this row's own יֹאכֵ֑ל; and the עשר root shared with this row's own לֶֽעָשִׁ֔יר and oshb:Eccl.5.12's opening word, each disclosed as texture that does not overturn the row's own hinge-comparison isolation. Test: collate.py byte-tier confirmation of each cited form; confirm the rationale no longer asserts a total absence of shared vocabulary.

rulings.grounds: CONFIRMED, and the row understates its own strength: רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה (oshb:Eccl.5.12) and רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה (oshb:Eccl.5.15) are byte-identical strings (verified by direct string comparison of the two spliced runs, accents included) -- the internal bracket claim is fully sound. UNDISCLOSED CROSS-SEAM DEVICE: תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.5.12, quoted inside this row's own opening formula) recurs at oshb:Eccl.5.17 as תַּֽחַת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ (byte tier at that verse; pointing differs from this row's own pausal form, so the recurrence is skeleton-tier, not byte-identical) immediately across this row's rear seam -- the eccl_device_inventory.json tachat_hashemesh inventory names both oshb:Eccl.5.12 and oshb:Eccl.5.17 as the chapter's two sites, and this row's own device_notes disclose only the adjacent paseq, not this refrain recurrence. Quote the pointed הִנֵּ֞ה (oshb:Eccl.5.17) rather than relying on the English "Behold" alone to argue the rear-seam pivot. Test: collate.py byte-tier confirmation of the added הנה quote; sweep.py skeleton-tier confirmation of the תחת השמש recurrence.

rulings.challenge_claim: The K/Q gloss at this row's own opening verse is attached to the wrong word ("his days" instead of "his life"); the row's own-span paseq goes undisclosed even though the preceding row explicitly flags it as belonging to this row; and the row's own-span under-the-sun refrain recurrence goes undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: GLOSS ERROR, independently re-derived: the row's own byte-tier run at oshb:Eccl.5.17 is מִסְפַּ֧ר יְמֵי חיו חַיָּ֛יו אֲשֶׁר -- ketiv חיו, qere חַיָּ֛יו ("his life"), immediately preceded by the UN-noted construct יְמֵי ("days of"). The row's rationale glosses the note as sitting on "his days" -- that is the preceding, note-free word; the actual note-bearing word means "his life," confirmed against the row's own spliced bytes. PASEQ ASYMMETRY: pmarks_Eccl.json records a paseq seg at Eccl.5.17 (MT); this row's own span opens at that verse, yet neither device_notes nor observed_substrate_signals mentions it, while the PRECEDING row (p02-006) explicitly discloses that same seg as "belonging to the following row's opening verse" -- the symmetry-completion rule is unmet on this row's own side. REFRAIN GAP: תַּֽחַת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ also falls at this row's own opening verse (oshb:Eccl.5.17, one of the book's tachat_hashemesh inventory sites), undisclosed here though the row cites the carpe_diem and kq inventories for the same verse.
rulings.remedy: Correct the K/Q gloss at oshb:Eccl.5.17 from "his days" to "his life" (the note sits on חיו/חַיָּ֛יו, not on יְמֵי). Add the paseq disclosure for this row's own opening verse oshb:Eccl.5.17 (pmarks_Eccl.json paseq inventory), completing the symmetry the preceding row already half-discloses. Add the תַּֽחַת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ under-the-sun disclosure for this row's own opening verse. Test: collate.py byte-tier confirmation of the corrected gloss; symmetry check that the paseq seg is now named by both the row that flagged it and the row it belongs to.
